IUT1.ThmB.content: Let k be a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field and X a hyperbolic curve over k, with tempered fundamental group Π^tp_X and étale fundamental group Π̂_X, so that Π^tp_X ⊆ Π̂_X and Π̂_X is the profinite completion of Π^tp_X. (1) A decomposition group in Π̂_X of a closed point or cusp of X (respectively an inertia group in Π̂_X of a cusp) is contained in Π^tp_X if and only if it is a decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively an inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp). (2) A Π̂_X-conjugate of Π^tp_X contains a decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively an inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp) if and only if it is equal to Π^tp_X.
explicit_hypotheses: k a mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field (MLF)
X a hyperbolic curve over k
Π^tp_X the tempered fundamental group and Π̂_X the étale fundamental group of X, relative to suitable basepoints, with the natural inclusion Π^tp_X ⊆ Π̂_X
IUT1.ThmB.conclusion: (1) For every decomposition group D ⊆ Π̂_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively inertia group I ⊆ Π̂_X of a cusp): D ⊆ Π^tp_X if and only if D is a decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively I ⊆ Π^tp_X if and only if I is an inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp). (2) For every γ ∈ Π̂_X: γ·Π^tp_X·γ^{-1} contains some decomposition group in Π^tp_X of a closed point or cusp (respectively some inertia group in Π^tp_X of a cusp) if and only if γ·Π^tp_X·γ^{-1} = Π^tp_X.
external_dependencies: [SemiAnbd] tempered groups and semi-graphs of anabelioids
obligations: Tempered fundamental groups are not in Mathlib.
ambiguities: Page 16 says Theorem B is essentially Corollary 2.5 (with Remark 2.5.2), and that the stable reduction hypothesis of Corollary 2.5 is unnecessary by Proposition 2.4 (iii). This is a relation between the two statements, not part of Theorem B; Theorem B itself has no stable reduction hypothesis.

IUT1.Thm2_6.content: Let F be a group containing a finite index subgroup G that is a free discrete group of finite rank or the fundamental group of a compact orientable topological surface of genus ≥ 2, and H ⊆ F an infinite subgroup. IUT1.Lem2_7.content: Let G be as in Theorem 2.6 (free of finite rank, or an orientable surface group of genus ≥ 2) and Ĝ its profinite completion. (i) Any subgroup of G generated by two elements is free. (ii) For x ∈ G, x ≠ 1, there is a finite index subgroup G_1 ⊆ G with x ∈ G_1 and x of nontrivial image in G_1^ab. (iii) For noncommuting x, y ∈ G there are a finite index subgroup G_1 ⊆ G and n ≥ 1 with x^n, y^n ∈ G_1 whose images in G_1^ab generate a free abelian subgroup of rank two. (iv) Every abelian subgroup of G is cyclic. (v) If T̂ ⊆ Ĝ is a closed subgroup and there is a continuous surjection Ĝ ↠ Ẑ inducing an isomorphism T̂ ≅ Ẑ, then T̂ is normally terminal in Ĝ. (vi) If G is nonabelian and N̂ = Ker(Ĝ ↠ Ĝ^ab), the centralizer Z_Ĝ(N̂) is trivial. (vii) In the notation of (vi), an automorphism of the profinite group Ĝ that preserves N̂ and restricts to the identity on N̂ is the identity.
explicit_hypotheses: G a free discrete group of finite rank or the fundamental group of a compact orientable surface of genus ≥ 2 (as in Theorem 2.6)
Ĝ the profinite completion of G
(ii): x ∈ G, x ≠ 1
(iii): x, y ∈ G noncommuting
(v): T̂ ⊆ Ĝ closed, with a continuous surjection Ĝ ↠ Ẑ inducing T̂ ≅ Ẑ
(vi), (vii): G nonabelian; (vii): α an automorphism of Ĝ preserving N̂ with α|_N̂ = id
IUT1.Lem2_7.conclusion: (i) two-generated subgroups are free; (ii) separation of x ≠ 1 in the abelianization of a finite index subgroup; (iii) x^n, y^n span a rank two free abelian subgroup of G_1^ab; (iv) abelian subgroups are cyclic; (v) T̂ is normally terminal in Ĝ; (vi) Z_Ĝ(N̂) = {1}; (vii) α = id.
obligations: Several parts are classical facts whose Mathlib coverage was not checked; surface groups are not defined in Mathlib.

IUT1.Cor2_8.content: Let Z be a hyperbolic curve over ℂ, Π_Z its usual topological fundamental group, Π̂_Z the profinite completion, H ⊆ Π_Z an infinite subgroup (such as a cuspidal inertia group), and γ ∈ Π̂_Z with γ·H·γ^{-1} ⊆ Π_Z. Then γ ∈ Π_Z·N_{Π̂_Z}(H), i.e. γ·H·γ^{-1} = δ·H·δ^{-1} for some δ ∈ Π_Z. If moreover H is nonabelian, then γ ∈ Π_Z.

IUT1.Sec0.PseudoMonoid.content: A topological pseudo-monoid is a topological space P with a continuous map S → P, S ⊆ P × P, such that there are a topological abelian group M (written multiplicatively) and an embedding ι : P ↪ M with S = {(a, b) | ι(a)·ι(b) ∈ ι(P)} and S → P the restriction of the group law. With M discrete, P is a pseudo-monoid. P is divisible if M, ι can be chosen so that every element of M has n-th roots for all n ≥ 1 and a ∈ ι(P) if and only if a^n ∈ ι(P); P is cyclotomic if M, ι can be chosen with μ_M ≅ Q/Z, μ_M ⊆ ι(P) and μ_M·ι(P) ⊆ ι(P).

IUT1.Sec0.Isomorph.content: An isomorph of an object is an isomorphic copy of it.

IUT1.Sec0.CategoryIsomorphism.content: For categories C, D, an isomorphism C → D means an isomorphism class of equivalences of categories C → D (differing from standard terminology); equivalently an isomorphism in the coarsification of the 2-category of small 1-categories relative to a suitable universe.

IUT1.Sec0.PolyMorphism.content: For objects A, B of a category C, a poly-morphism A → B is a collection of morphisms A → B, that is, a subset of the set of morphisms A → B.
obligations: The Lean declaration is a definition; there is no proof to verify.
ambiguities: The empty subset is allowed by the wording 'a subset'.

IUT1.Sec0.PolyIsomorphism.content: A poly-morphism all of whose members are isomorphisms is a poly-isomorphism.
obligations: The Lean declaration is a definition; there is no proof to verify.

IUT1.Sec0.PolyAutomorphism.content: A poly-isomorphism A ⥲ A (with A = B) is a poly-automorphism.
obligations: The Lean declaration is a definition; there is no proof to verify.

IUT1.Sec0.FullPolyIsomorphism.content: The full poly-isomorphism A ⥲ B is the poly-morphism given by the collection of all isomorphisms A ⥲ B.
obligations: The Lean declaration is a definition; there is no proof to verify.

IUT1.Sec0.PolyMorphismComposite.content: The composite of a poly-morphism {f_i : A → B}_{i∈I} with a poly-morphism {g_j : B → C}_{j∈J} is the poly-morphism given by the set {g_j ∘ f_i}_{(i,j)∈I×J}, multiplicities ignored.
obligations: The Lean declaration is a definition; there is no proof to verify.
ambiguities: Lean composes in diagrammatic order: g_j ∘ f_i is f_i ≫ g_j.

IUT1.Sec0.Capsule.content: A capsule of objects of a category C is a finite collection {A_j}_{j∈J} of objects of C indexed by a finite index set J; it is a |J|-capsule, and π_0({A_j}_{j∈J}) = J.
obligations: The Lean declaration is a definition; there is no proof to verify.
The |J|-capsule terminology and π_0 are IUT.PaperI.Capsule.IsNCapsule and IUT.PaperI.Capsule.π₀.
ambiguities: The index set is a Lean type in Type with a Fintype instance.

IUT1.Sec0.CapsuleMorphism.content: A morphism of capsules {A_j}_{j∈J} → {A'_{j'}}_{j'∈J'} consists of an injection ι : J ↪ J' and, for each j ∈ J, a morphism A_j → A'_{ι(j)}; capsules of objects of C form a category Capsule(C).
obligations: IUT.PaperI.Capsule.Hom, Hom.id and Hom.comp state the morphisms, identities and composition, but the category laws of Capsule(C) are not proved in Lean, so this record is not linked to a Lean declaration.

IUT1.Sec0.CapsuleFullPolyMorphism.content: A capsule-full poly-morphism {A_j}_{j∈J} → {A'_{j'}}_{j'∈J'} is the poly-morphism associated to a fixed injection ι : J ↪ J' consisting of the capsule morphisms given by collections of arbitrary isomorphisms A_j ⥲ A'_{ι(j)}, j ∈ J.
obligations: The Lean declaration is a definition; there is no proof to verify.

IUT1.Sec0.CapsuleFullPolyIsomorphism.content: A capsule-full poly-isomorphism is a capsule-full poly-morphism whose associated injection between index sets is a bijection.
obligations: IUT.PaperI.Capsule.IsCapsuleFullPolyIso states only the bijectivity condition on the injection ι, not the whole definition, so the record is not linked.

IUT1.Sec0.FiniteEtaleCategory.content: For a connected noetherian algebraic stack X that is generically scheme-like, B(X) is the category of finite étale coverings of X (with morphisms over X); for a noetherian ring A, B(A) = B(Spec(A)); B(X)^0 ⊆ B(X) is the subcategory of connected objects.
obligations: Algebraic stacks are not in Mathlib.

IUT1.Sec0.TemperedGroup.content: For a topological group Π, B^temp(Π) is the category of countable discrete sets with continuous Π-action and Π-equivariant maps. Π is tempered if it is an inverse limit of an inverse system of surjections of countable discrete topological groups. A category equivalent to B^temp(Π) with Π tempered is a connected temperoid; then C ≃ (C^0)^⊤. For Galois-countable Π, Π is reconstructed up to inner automorphism from B^temp(Π) or B^temp(Π)^0, which defines π_1(C), π_1(C^0) for a Galois-countable connected temperoid C.
obligations: Tempered groups and temperoids are not in Mathlib; the reconstruction of π_1 cites Remark 2.5.3 (i), (T1), (T5).

IUT1.Sec0.TemperoidMorphism.content: For connected temperoids C_1, C_2, a morphism C_1 → C_2 is an isomorphism class of functors C_2 → C_1 preserving finite limits and countable colimits; a morphism C_1^0 → C_2^0 is a morphism (C_1^0)^⊤ → (C_2^0)^⊤. For Galois-countable tempered Π_1, Π_2 there are natural bijections between continuous outer homomorphisms Π_1 → Π_2, morphisms B^temp(Π_1) → B^temp(Π_2), and morphisms B^temp(Π_1)^0 → B^temp(Π_2)^0.
obligations: Temperoids are not in Mathlib.
ambiguities: Page 35 notes this differs slightly from [SemiAnbd] Definition 3.1 (iii).

IUT1.Sec0.AbstractlyEquivalent.content: Isomorphism classes of functors φ : C_1 → C_2 and φ' : C'_1 → C'_2 are abstractly equivalent if there are isomorphisms α_i : C_i ⥲ C'_i (i = 1, 2) with φ' ∘ α_1 = α_2 ∘ φ; the same terminology applies to morphisms of (connected) temperoids and of their subcategories of connected objects.

IUT1.Sec0.Valuations.content: NF, MLF, CAF abbreviate number field, mixed-characteristic nonarchimedean local field, complex archimedean field; Primes is the set of prime numbers. For a number field F, V(F) = V(F)^arc ∪ V(F)^non is the set of valuations (places) of F; F_v is the completion at v; an element is integral at v if of norm ≤ 1; for a Galois extension L of F, L_v is the completion at a valuation of L over v; p_v is the residue characteristic for nonarchimedean v and, for archimedean v, the positive real element of F_v with natural logarithm 1 (p_v = e). These notations extend to infinite extensions of Q by projective or inductive limits.
